lane: kama round 27 attempt 3, w1a3 evidence seats
claim_served: Mined mistake fix (corpus/lessons/round-27.md:92, Mistakes row 1): show the file-size cap (ulimit -f, i.e. RLIMIT_FSIZE) is able to fail a runaway self-appending fixture.

guard.note: every harness and the capture wrapper set ulimit -f 1048576 (1 GiB per file) and ulimit -c 0 before any fixture write; harnesses run under timeout (300 s / 120 s)

units.meaning: bash's ulimit -f is in 1024-byte blocks; 2048 -> 2 MiB, 20480 -> 20 MiB

fixture.loop: BLOB = open(__file__,'rb').read(); while True: open(__file__,'ab').write(BLOB)  (linear self-append of the file's own bytes)
fixture.marker: two-line MARKER-A3-FIXTURE-BOUND-DEMO snippet at the file head, mirroring the incident's repeated two-line MARKER
fixture.separate_log: MiB crossings are written to $PROGRESS_LOG, a file Python never imports and never reads back; the fixture is not on any sys.path and nothing appends to it except the loop

switches.A3_SIG_DFL=1: signal.signal(SIGXFSZ, SIG_DFL) before the loop; changes signal disposition only, not the loop
switches.A3_SWALLOW=1: catch OSError around the self-append and keep looping (loop body otherwise identical)

signal_disposition.decoded: bit 24 set = signal 25 = SIGXFSZ ignored by bash 5.3.20; children inherit SIG_IGN across exec
signal_disposition.trap_dash_SIGXFSZ: SigIgn still 0000000001000000; child python handler still SIG_IGN
signal_disposition.consequence: a plain `( ulimit -f N; timeout t python3 fixture.py )` under bash does NOT kill the writer by SIGXFSZ; the kernel clamps the crossing write and Python raises OSError(EFBIG, errno 27). Exit 153 requires the writer to restore SIG_DFL (or a writer that does not inherit the ignore).

runs.label: A0
runs.role: assignment (a), exact literal writer (no signal reset)
runs.command: ( ulimit -f 2048; export PROGRESS_LOG=A0.log A3_SIG_DFL=0; exec timeout 60 python3 fixture.py ) >A0.stdout 2>A0.stderr
runs.exit_meaning: uncaught OSError [Errno 27] File too large (EFBIG); SIGXFSZ ignored so no signal death
runs.stderr_excerpt: Traceback ... File "fixture.py", line 127 ... OSError: [Errno 27] File too large
runs.conclusion: the run loop stopped at exactly the cap and the process exited

runs.label: A1
runs.role: assignment (a), death path (SIGXFSZ restored to default)
runs.command: ( ulimit -f 2048; export PROGRESS_LOG=A1.log A3_SIG_DFL=1; exec timeout 60 python3 fixture.py ) >A1.stdout 2>A1.stderr
runs.exit_meaning: 128 + 25 = SIGXFSZ (File size limit exceeded); writer terminated by the kernel
runs.stderr_excerpt: timeout: the monitored command dumped core (RLIMIT_CORE=0, no core file written)
runs.conclusion: (a) shows the cap: exit 153 with final size == cap

runs.label: B1
runs.role: assignment (b), same loop, outer safety bound 20 MiB
runs.command: ( ulimit -f 20480; export PROGRESS_LOG=B1.log A3_SIG_DFL=1; exec timeout 5 python3 fixture.py ) >B1.stdout 2>B1.stderr
runs.conclusion: same loop grew past 2 MiB and stopped only at the 20 MiB cap; the 2 MiB stop in (a) was the cap, not the loop or the clock

runs.label: C0
runs.role: identical-timeout control: same loop, same timeout 5, only the cap differs from B1
runs.command: ( ulimit -f 2048; export PROGRESS_LOG=C0.log A3_SIG_DFL=1; exec timeout 5 python3 fixture.py ) >C0.stdout 2>C0.stderr
runs.conclusion: at equal timeout (5 s) the 2 MiB cap still stops the file at 2,097,152 while B1 reaches 20,971,520; the timeout is not the confound

runs.label: E
runs.role: supplementary: swallowing writer with SIGXFSZ at default
runs.command: ( ulimit -f 2048; export PROGRESS_LOG=E.log A3_SIG_DFL=1 A3_SWALLOW=1; exec timeout 3 python3 fixture.py ) >E.stdout 2>E.stderr
runs.conclusion: with SIG_DFL the signal terminates during the write, so the except never runs; the cap wins before Python can swallow it

runs.label: E2
runs.role: supplementary: swallowing writer with bash's inherited SIG_IGN
runs.command: ( ulimit -f 2048; export PROGRESS_LOG=E2.log A3_SIG_DFL=0 A3_SWALLOW=1; exec timeout 3 python3 fixture.py ) >E2.stdout 2>E2.stderr
runs.conclusion: writer survived and logged 889,000 EFBIG errors in 3 s; the file stayed pinned at exactly the cap; timeout, not ulimit, stopped the loop

supplementary_shell_writers.label: D

supplementary_shell_writers.observation: with a seed large enough to reach the cap, every later cat write fails EFBIG; the file is pinned at exactly the cap while the loop spins until timeout

cases.case: open('cap.bin','ab') on a file already at exactly 2097152, no write
cases.note: open itself never raises at the cap
OSError [Errno 27] raises from close(), not from write(): the 10 bytes were buffered
'Exception ignored while finalizing file' OSError EFBIG; an unflushed first failure can be dropped at interpreter exit
the crossing write is clamped to exactly the cap; the remainder raises EFBIG at close

efbig_site_probe.conclusion: the cap clamps the crossing write to exactly the limit and surfaces the error at flush/close; with buffered io the first EFBIG may appear one flush later than the write that caused it, and the file is bounded regardless

scope_limits: Establishes RLIMIT_FSIZE effectiveness on a generic linear self-append writer; it does not reconstruct the incident's exact writer or the MARKER alias (the critic's point is accepted).

The detector() helper in run-demo.sh:42-43 only echoes <label>_size<=<bound>=YES/NO and always exits 0, so the printed B1_size<=2097152=NO is a reporting aid, not the CORPUS.md:179-183 red-before command; the gate-shaped artifact is strict_red_before_pair (red detector exit 3 with committed failure text, fixed detector exit 0, only ulimit -f differs).

No uncapped (red) arm was run: the uncapped behavior is the incident itself (262,699,483,136 bytes, /fast full). The 20 MiB row stands in for the red arm under an outer safety bound; the C0/B1 pair holds the timeout constant so the only delta is the cap.

A soft RLIMIT_FSIZE is inherited by children and can be raised by a child up to the hard limit; with both limits at the cap (as set here) the child cannot raise it. Evidence here measures soft=hard=cap.

bash 5.3.20 leaves SIGXFSZ ignored in children, so 153 is the expected exit only when the writer restores SIG_DFL; otherwise the cap surfaces as OSError EFBIG (exit 1) or, if the writer swallows it, as a bounded file plus a spinning process.
